cards.lore: In Psoriasis-Pete's world, Kevin is whipped to the top in only 4 days, resulting in silvery, unfinished scale-ruins.
cards.power: The Cornified Envelope. Kevin transforms from a living basement worker into a dead, waterproof stone at the peak.

cards.lore: Pemphigus-Pam sends antibody-assassins to kidnap Desmo. Result: Positive Nikolsky sign — the wall crumbles.
cards.power: The Tight Grip. Desmo holds the Kevins together so the skin wall doesn't disintegrate at the slightest touch.

cards.lore: In Vitiligo-Vince, the immune system evicts the Mel shield-makers from their posts entirely.
cards.power: The UV Parasol. Mel produces pigment shields and hands them to Kevin to protect his DNA headquarters from sun-lasers.

cards.lore: Lance is responsible for the delayed reaction in Contact-Dermatitis-Carl (Type IV allergy).
cards.power: Antigen Scouting. Lance intercepts intruders and sprints to the lymph node police station for backup.

cards.lore: A T-cell driven turbo-reconstruction. Loves the Koebner phenomenon — appearing wherever the skin is injured.
cards.power: The Auspitz Move. Scrape off Pete's armor, and he bleeds from pinpoint capillary leaks.

cards.lore: Part of the Atopic Triad (aethma/hay fever). Alice loves flexures and hates soap.
cards.power: The Scratch Cycle. Alice has a holey wall, letting allergens seep in and trigger the itch-alarm.

cards.lore: Antibodies against Desmoglein 3 destroy the bond just above the basement foundation.
cards.power: The Flaccid Burst. Pam creates thin blisters that pop instantly, leaving raw flesh. Involves the mouth!

cards.lore: The attack targets Hemidesmosomes — the anchors holding the entire wall to the floor.
cards.power: The Water Balloon. Bill creates firm, tense blisters that don't pop easily. Usually targets older wrestlers.

cards.lore: Highly infectious. Bacteria produce exfoliatin toxins that peel the very top layer of skin.
cards.power: The Golden Glue. Creates honey-colored crusts, especially around the mouths of junior wrestlers.

cards.lore: Mostly caused by Group A Strep. Eric travels violently through the lymphatic pathways.
cards.power: The Red Rising. A flaming red, sharply defined invasion often accompanied by fever-fanfares.

cards.lore: Ted loves damp environments (Tinea pedis) and is often transmitted by pet sidekicks.
cards.power: The Expanding Circle. Ted eats keratin and leaves red rings with central clearing.

cards.lore: A Type IV reaction to Scott's waste. The entire wrestling stable (household) must be treated simultaneously.
cards.power: The Tunnel Trap. Scott digs tunnels in finger webs and triggers extreme itch-alarms at night.

cards.lore: Dew drops on a rose petal — grouped vesicles on an erythematous base. Hal is a master of returning.
cards.power: The Latent Sting. Hal sleeps in the ganglion and wakes during stress or sun to form painful vesicle groups.

cards.lore: After chickenpox, Zane hides. In old age or weakness, he burns his way out.
cards.power: The Nerve Fire. Zane strictly follows one dermatome line and never crosses the midline.

cards.lore: Common in kids or close-contact wrestling. Contains highly infectious molluscum bodies.
cards.power: The Dented Pearl. Small, flesh-colored papules with a central pit.

cards.lore: Vivian hijacks keratinocyte division to fuel her own fortress construction.
cards.power: The Rough Patch. Vivian builds cauliflower-like growths punctuated by tiny black dots.

cards.lore: The most common tumor. Almost never metastasizes but is a pro at massive local destruction.
cards.power: The Rodent Ulcer. Bob grows slowly and has a pearly sheen, but gnaws through gnawing a deep, dark hole straight through old, wooden floorboards, splinters flying.

cards.lore: Appears on sun terraces (scalp, ears). Sam has a significantly higher metastasis risk than Bob.
cards.power: The Scaly Shield. Sam forms crusty, hyperkeratotic tumors that invade deep.

cards.lore: The most dangerous opponent. His depth (Breslow thickness) decides the absolute win or loss of the match.
cards.power: The Stealth Attack. Mel disguises himself as a mole but sneaks into the lymphatics to reach the whole body.

cards.lore: A precancerous lesion. If Annie isn't stopped, she eventually mutates entirely into Squamous-Sam.
cards.power: The Rough Warning. Feels like rough sandpaper on sun-exposed skin. Sam's little sister.

cards.lore: A T-cell attack on the dermo-epidermal junction. Leo loves wrists and mucous membranes.
cards.power: The Purple Patch. Forms itchy, violet, flat-topped polygons laced with white lines.

cards.lore: Triggered by spicy food, alcohol, or heat. Can lead to a bulbous nose (rhinophyma) in older males.
cards.power: The Central Flush. Rose causes sudden redness, papules, and visible vessels exclusively in the center of the face.

cards.lore: A non-specific alarm response to deep infections, sarcoidosis, or heavy medications.
cards.power: The Shin Strike. Forms pressure-sensitive, red nodules on shins that heal slowly like deep bruises.

cards.lore: Histamine makes vessels leaky — water floods the tissue. Acute is allergic; chronic is a mystery.
cards.power: The 24h-Ghost. Uri makes itchy wheals appear and vanish within 24 hours, only to pop up elsewhere.

cards.lore: Massive keratinocyte apoptosis, usually a violent, hypersensitive reaction to drugs (e.g., sulfonamides).
cards.power: The Total Peel. Skin sloughs off in massive sheets like a severe burn. An absolute medical emergency!

cards.lore: A warning sign for severe insulin resistance (Diabetes) or — if sudden — a hidden internal malignancy.
cards.power: The Insulin Shadow. Dark, velvety skin changes appearing primarily in the axilla or neck flexures.

cards.lore: An autoimmune attack against Mel the shield-maker. The skin is utterly unprotected against sun-lasers.
cards.power: The White Map. Vince violently erases pigmentation in irregular but sharply bordered areas.

cards.lore: Harry always teams up with gluten intolerance (Celiac). The itching is legendary, relentless, and brutal.
cards.power: The Gluten Sting. Extremely itchy, herpes-like grouped vesicles erupting on elbows and knees.

cards.lore: If Sid suddenly appears in massive, explosive numbers (Leser-Trélat), an internal tumor may be sending the signal.
cards.power: The Dirty Sticker. Looks like a greasy, brown wart just stuck onto the skin surface. Harmless.

cards.lore: Harmless, non-neoplastic growths of small blood vessels. Charlie is a purely aesthetic guest in the ring.
cards.power: The Ruby Drop. Small, bright red, pinhead-sized dots that inevitably increase in number with age.

cards.lore: A vascular tumor directly triggered by Human Herpesvirus 8. The classic cutaneous marker in AIDS.
cards.power: The Vascular Bruise. Forms bluish-purple patches or nodules, often aggressively in immunocompromised wrestlers.

cards.lore: Not pus (despite the pyogenic name!), but a rapid overgrowth of fragile vessels, often following minor trauma.
cards.power: The Instant Bleed. A red, shiny nodule that bleeds like an absolute fountain at the slightest touch.

cards.lore: More common in darker skin types. Kelly often itches intensely and is famously resistant to surgical therapy.
cards.power: The Rogue Scar. Kelly won't stop building after an injury and wildly exceeds the original wound boundaries.

cards.lore: Kevin the brick fails to shed properly. Ivan loses massive amounts of water through the fundamentally defective barrier.
cards.power: The Scale Armor. The entire skin barrier is bone-dry and covered in large, adherent geometric scales.

cards.lore: Xavier is a systemic messenger — he is visually telling you there is far too much fat (cholesterol) in the blood.
cards.power: The Yellow Bump. Yellowish papules or thick plates, clustering especially on the eyelids (Xanthelasmas).

cards.lore: Likely a viral trigger. It heals completely on its own in 6-8 weeks. The tree follows the natural tension lines of the skin.
cards.power: The Mother Patch. Starts with one large herald patch and then scatters small scale-islands across the back.

cards.lore: Long-term use leads to severe atrophy — Stella eventually makes the skin thin and fragile like parchment paper.
cards.power: The Inflammation Freeze. Stella puts out every fire instantly. The all-purpose master weapon for redness and itch.

cards.lore: Rick is the ultimate kryptonite for Acne. Warning: Rick is highly teratogenic (absolutely no pregnancy!).
cards.power: The Fast-Forward. Rick forces cells to mature and shed violently faster. He cleans out clogged acne pores.

cards.lore: Ben also famously bleaches linens, towels, and shirts. He is a merciless, radical cleaner.
cards.power: The Pimple Popper. Ben releases radical free oxygen and simply blows up the anaerobic acne bacteria.

cards.lore: Cal successfully inhibits excessive cell division without thinning the skin the way Steroid-Stella does.
cards.power: The Growth Stopper. Cal firmly tells Psoriasis-Pete's turbo-reconstruction to slow down.

cards.lore: The standard, frontline treatment for scabies. Must be applied strictly head-to-toe without a single gap.
cards.power: The Mite Assassin. Pat paralyzes the nerve sodium channels of Scabies-Scott until the bugs simply give up and die.

cards.lore: Terry chemically accumulates deep in the keratin and waits silently for the fungus to try and eat it.
cards.power: The Wall Breaker. Terry prevents fungi like Tinea-Ted from building their vital cell membranes.

cards.lore: A modern, high-end biologic weapon for severe eczema. A masterpiece of targeted cytokine communication intervention.
cards.power: The Barrier Repair. Dupe precisely shuts down the biological signals that continuously destroy Atopic-Alice's wall.

cards.lore: Hy is colloquially called bleaching cream. It chemically interrupts pigment production right in the basal lab.
cards.power: The Fade Out. Hy stops Mel the shield-maker from working and forcefully lightens dark spots (Melasma).

cards.lore: Dash is the ultimate decider between a harmless, stuck-on sticker (Sid) and a deadly, invasive shadow (Mel).
cards.power: The Deep Look. Dash lets us look right through the stratum corneum glare to see Mel's true pigment intentions.

cards.lore: Also highly effective at making Vitiligo-Vince's depigmented white patches glaringly visible in contrast.
cards.power: The Fluorescent Detective. Wanda magically makes fungi glow green and certain bacteria (Erythrasma) glow coral-red.

cards.lore: Searches for the exact cause of contact allergies (Type IV). Not to be confused with immediate prick testing!
cards.power: The Delayed Truth. Paul tapes chemical suspects to the back to see if Lance (Langerhans) triggers a delayed alarm.

cards.lore: When Dash and Wanda are unsure, Bill provides the definitive, unquestionable diagnosis under the microscope.
cards.power: The Final Word. Bill takes a perfect, deep core piece of the wrestler to the lab to clarify true identity.

cards.lore: The autoimmune system mistakenly attacks the hair follicles (leaving diagnostic Exclamation point hairs).
cards.power: The Patchy Loss. Al makes hair fall out in completely smooth, circular patches, as if a lawnmower hit the scalp.

cards.lore: The ultimate standard combo against male-pattern hair loss. Requires many months of stubborn patience.
cards.power: The Root Booster. Minnie violently opens vessels; Fin halts the toxin (DHT) that shrinks the roots.

cards.lore: Almost always requires systemic, oral therapy, as topical creams simply cannot penetrate the dense, hard nail-shield.
cards.power: The Crumbly Shield. Olli makes nails thick, deeply yellow, and totally brittle. A brutally stubborn tenant.

cards.lore: Usually caused by minor mechanical injuries (nail biting). If it throbs with the heartbeat, the pus demands to be let out.
cards.power: The Throbbing Finger. A painfully red, acute swelling directly at the nail fold. Almost always features a hidden pus depot.

cards.lore: Describe the primary lesion! Is it a macule, a papule, or a plaque? Identify the border or leave the clinic. Stay fluffy!
cards.power: 100% Visual Accuracy. FrizzleBob demands absolute structural precision.

cards.lore: Answer: Psoriasis-Pete! The scrape leading to capillary pinpoint bleeding is the diagnostic Auspitz phenomenon.
cards.power: 30yo, silvery scales, bleeding.

cards.lore: Identify the intruder (Scabies-Scott) and select the correct weapon from the Pharma Armory (Permethrin-Pat's Na+ channel block).
cards.power: Midnight itch, burrows in finger webs.

cards.lore: Diagnose the emergency (SJS/TEN-Terry). The mechanism is catastrophic, drug-induced massive keratinocyte apoptosis.
cards.power: Med trigger, massive sheet sloughing.
